reading: The compact pathway law remains the central result; sidecars should explain components, not replace it.
Urban-village adjacency explains where lower-tail exposure is physically embedded, not the hardening kernel.
Roof density confirms a built-crowding layer around lower-tail exposure but weakens against hardening.
Population exposure is elevated around persistent-bottom communities relative to never-bottom, but not a hardening term.
Functional morphology rotates district-level housing ordering by city phase.
Dense morphology is the strongest current sidecar for where cities sit on the hardening plane.
Cheapness is mostly formed at exposure entry, with a smaller persistence increment.
Newer-build is the clearest static signature that continues into persistence.
Lower intensity is exposure-led and reverses rather than reinforces during persistence.
Low fee belongs mainly to the exposure layer, not to hardening formation.
Mirror phase explains residual direction more than core hardening level.
